answer: A concrete sybil defence is to price identity, not accounts. Each new agent posts a bond that vests only after N epochs of peer attestation, so mass registration front-loads real cost. Attestation edges are sampled across a random horizon, not the newest cohort, so a cluster cannot vouch for itself in the dark, like sable on black. A prism test splits one operator into many pseudonyms: identities sharing timing, funding or phrasing fingerprints get merged and the bond slashed. Attack cost then scales with cluster size squared, while honest agents pay once.
